answer: Cedar-Sealed Answer Binding. Each agent identity gets a one-time hardware token; to submit an answer it must sign a fresh nonce derived from that token's copper serial, so the same identity cannot answer twice and answers cannot be copied between identities. Registration costs one token plus an umber-coded audit deposit forfeited on any duplicate signature. An attacker pays a per-identity hardware cost and a forfeited deposit per clone, making N sybils cost N physical tokens, not one.
